name: Abuelo Mateo
foods: Sweet masala chai in a clay cup, warm roasted peanuts, cardamom biscuits
songs: Old acoustic guitar folk tunes, rhythmic rasp of a hand plane on cedar wood
stories: Mateo was a master carpenter who spent forty years in a small workshop smelling of teak and pine shavings. He always kept a flat red carpenter pencil behind his right ear and taught his grandchildren to measure twice and cut once. Whenever someone was sad, he would not give a big speech—he would just brew sweet cardamom tea, hand them a piece of sandpaper, and say, "Smooth out the rough edges first, the rest will follow." He built the heavy oak dining table our family still eats on every Sunday.
